metadata.title: [CHORE][SECURITY]: Pin urllib3 and python-multipart to latest versions
metadata.author: ChrisPC-39

description:
## 📝 Summary
`urllib3` and `python-multipart` are transitive dependencies that are installed with older versions. This PR ensures the latest versions of these packages are installed in the project:
1. urllib3>=2.6.3 (previously was 2.5.0, installed by `requests`)
2. python-multipart>=0.0.22 (previously was 0.0.20, installed by `mcp`)

---

commits.message:

commits.message:
chore(deps): update dependency versions and add CVE references

Run update_dependencies.py to bump transitive versions. Add inline
CVE and Dependabot references to urllib3 and python-multipart pins.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix(tools): preserve inline comments in update_dependencies.py

The script was stripping inline comments (e.g. CVE references) because
tomlkit stores array-item comments on internal _ArrayItemGroup objects,
not on the string item trivia. Extract comments from the original array
groups before processing and re-attach them via add_line(comment=...).

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
chore(deps): simplify transitive pin comments and remove block comments

commits.message:
fix(deps): restore protobuf <7.0.0 cap for grpcio-reflection compatibility

83e16ea09 blindly bumped protobuf to >=7.34.0, undoing the deliberate
pin from 2e85fbe24. grpcio-reflection 1.78.x caps protobuf at <7.0.0,
making resolution unsatisfiable on Python 3.13.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix(deps): cap schemathesis <4.11.0 for pytest-md-report compatibility

schemathesis 4.11.0 requires pytest>=9, but pytest-md-report 0.7.0
caps at pytest<9. No newer pytest-md-report exists yet. Revert to
the previous working range until the conflict is resolved upstream.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
